items.title: Bill Huntington Interview, 1961-12-27
items.q: He felt that his brother had been the musician of the family, his brother and his father, Billy.

ctx.x: Sure. Yeah, just talk. Just say anything that comes to your mind. No, I'd rather not do that. . .

Well, uh, when I was about fifteen, uh, uh, actually through the efforts of Alvin Purnell. You see, I used to sit in with George Lewis and Alvin Purnell had a thing going where he'd play passing chords. And, uh, I was told when I was a kid that I had some kind of fantastic gear. I was some kind of child prodigy or something, you see. And so, uh, I'd hear all the things he was playing. And I'd tell Lawrence, why aren't you playing the same chords Alton's playing? You know, they sound like they're fitting more into…
Who did you like when you started playing? You mentioned Bonk, and then there must have been some other musicians. You said you met a lot on the mind.
